newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa arrivals seen picking up this month.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa arrivals seen picking up this month.

text.p: Cocoa arrivals in Ivory Coast reached 285,000 tonnes by end-November and are set to pick up as December contracts fall due, exporters and trade analysts said.
Cocoa had been coming into Abidjan and San Pedro, Ivory Coast's second port, at a rate of about 40,000 tonnes a week, against about 50,000 towards the end of November last year, they said.

"There could be even more as the figures for Abidjan are not clear," said one exporter, putting the total closer to 300,000 tonnes. Volumes were down 20 percent on last year but would pick up this week, he added.
Exporters expected arrivals to rise up to December 15 before a Christmas lull. Around 250,000-300,000 tonnes were expected to be declared in December.
One crop analyst said 1995/96 arrivals had reached 338,000 tonnes by the end of November and 668,000 by the year's end, so figures to date showed only a 15 percent drop on last year.

"The figures are difficult to compare because of last year's shipping freight rate dispute, which slowed early arrivals, and different crop profiles," he said. "Even so, the picture is really not that bad."
Ivory Coast opened its 1996/97 cocoa marketing season on October 24.

Arrivals at Abidjan would also pick up as cocoa started to come in from eastern regions, exporters said. Cocoa from the less productive eastern areas usually arrived later than supplies from the west.
San Pedro exporters and buyers last week said total arrivals could be down by as much as 25 percent in 1996/97 after a record 1.2 million tonne harvest in 1995/96.
They estimated arrivals to end-November at around 250,000 tonnes, but Abidjan-based exporters said that figure was too low.
Smuggling out of Ivory Coast was not seen as having much impact on arrivals.

"Arrivals will be affected, but not much," said one exporter, referring to a newspaper report of smuggling into Guinea. "It's difficult to put a figure on it (smuggling) but it was stopped last year," he added,
Cocoa was fetching 700 CFA per kilo in Guinea against 315 CFA per kilo in Ivory Coast, said the opposition daily La Voie.
San Pedro port stocks had fallen from November 26 levels of more than least 40,000 tonnes after large shipments, port sources said.
Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan recently put total Ivory Coast 1996/97 production at 950,000 tonnes.
